\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Basic}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.Basic
\section{Overview}
Finite probability products are equipped with coordinate conditional expectations, an orthogonal decomposition, noise operators, and influences. The probability weights may differ between coordinates and are strictly positive.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Alternating subset-intersection quadratic form]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signedIntersectionEnergy}
\leanok
For a finite set $S$ and a real function $g$ on finite subsets of an ambient set, define $E_S(g)=\sum_{A,B\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|A|}(-1)^{|S|-|B|}g(A\cap B)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Insertion recurrence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signedIntersectionEnergy_insert}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signedIntersectionEnergy}
\difficulty{5}
For a finite set $S$, an element $i\notin S$, and a real function $g$ on finite subsets, put $E_T(g)=\sum_{A,B\subseteq T}(-1)^{|T|-|A|}(-1)^{|T|-|B|}g(A\cap B)$. Then $E_{S\cup\{i\}}(g)=E_S(T\mapsto g(T\cup\{i\}))-E_S(g)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subset energy cancellation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_powerset_signed_inter}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signedIntersectionEnergy, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signedIntersectionEnergy_insert}
\difficulty{5}
For a finite set $U$ and a real function $g$ on finite subsets, put $E_S(g)=\sum_{A,B\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|A|}(-1)^{|S|-|B|}g(A\cap B)$. Then $\sum_{S\subseteq U}E_S(g)=g(U)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite probability product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct}
\leanok
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, a finite probability product consists of finite sets $\Omega_i$ for $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and real weights $w_i(a)>0$ satisfying $\sum_{a\in\Omega_i}w_i(a)=1$. The coordinate sets and weights may depend on $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product outcomes]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point}
\leanok
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$. Its outcome space is $\Omega=\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\Omega_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product probability mass]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, with coordinate weights $w_i$. The mass of $x\in\prod_i\Omega_i$ is $m(x)=\prod_iw_i(x_i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product expectation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, with product masses $m(x)$. For $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$, define $\mathbb E_Pf=\sum_xm(x)f(x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Event indicator]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.indicator}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and let $A$ be an event in its outcome space. Its indicator $\mathbf1_A$ equals $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Event probability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.indicator}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and let $A$ be an event in its outcome space. Define $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real moment norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $q\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $\|f\|_{q,P}=(\mathbb E_P|f|^q)^{1/q}$ using real powers and division; for $q>0$ this is the usual moment expression.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product variance]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.variance}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $\operatorname{Var}_P(f)=\mathbb E_P(f-\mathbb E_Pf)^2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate dependence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.DependsOn}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Say that $f$ depends only on $S$ if $f(x)=f(y)$ whenever $x_i=y_i$ for every $i\in S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate conditional expectation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $E_Sf(x)=\mathbb E_{Y\sim P}f(z)$, where $z_i=x_i$ for $i\in S$ and $z_i=Y_i$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal component]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Its $S$-component is $f_S=\sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}E_Tf$, where $E_T$ conditions on the coordinates in $T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product degree bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.HasDegreeLE}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. The predicate that $f$ has degree at most $k$ means that every orthogonal component $f_S$ with $|S|>k$ vanishes identically.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Low degree projection]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.lowDegree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $f^{\le k}(x)=\sum_{|S|\le k}f_S(x)$, where $f_S$ is the orthogonal component indexed by $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product spectral noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $T_\rho f(x)=\sum_S\rho^{|S|}f_S(x)$, where $f_S$ are the orthogonal components and the powers have natural exponents.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate Laplacian]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a coordinate $i$, and $f:\prod_j\Omega_j\to\mathbb R$. Define $L_if=f-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}f$, where $E_S$ conditions on the coordinates in $S$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.laplacian}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a coordinate $i$, and $f:\prod_j\Omega_j\to\mathbb R$. Define $I_i(f)=\mathbb E_P(L_if)^2$, where $L_if$ subtracts the conditional expectation over coordinate $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Total product influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.totalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.influence}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $I(f)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(f)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stable product influence]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stableInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, a coordinate $i$, and $f:\prod_j\Omega_j\to\mathbb R$. Define $I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\sum_{S\ni i}\rho^{|S|-1}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2$, with natural exponents, including $\rho=0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Product noise stability]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stability}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. Define $\operatorname{Stab}_\rho(f)=\mathbb E_P[fT_\rho f]$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform atom lower bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound}
\leanok
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with coordinate weights $w_i$ and let $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. The atom lower bound $\lambda$ means that $\lambda\le w_i(a)$ for every coordinate $i$ and outcome $a\in\Omega_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean product functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\prod_i\Omega_i\to\mathbb R$. The Boolean-valued predicate means $f(x)\in\{-1,1\}$ at every outcome $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product mass normalization]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass_sum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, with product masses $m(x)$. Then $\sum_xm(x)=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exchange of independent samples]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_swap_samples}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $F:\Omega\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$, where $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$. For independent $X,Y\sim P$, let $X\mathbin{\star_S}Y$ keep $X_i$ on $S$ and $Y_i$ elsewhere; then $\mathbb E F(X\mathbin{\star_S}Y,Y\mathbin{\star_S}X)=\mathbb EF(X,Y)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of constants]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass_sum}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $c\in\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P[c]=c$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of linear combinations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, let $s$ be a finite index set, and let $a_j\in\mathbb R$ and $F_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P\sum_{j\in s}a_jF_j=\sum_{j\in s}a_j\mathbb E_PF_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Composition of conditional expectations]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_comp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_swap_samples}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S,T\subseteq[n]$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. For coordinate conditional expectations, $E_S(E_Tf)(x)=E_{S\cap T}f(x)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Self-adjoint conditional expectation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_swap_samples}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $S\subseteq[n]$, and $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For conditional expectation $E_S$ onto $S$, $\mathbb E_P[fE_Sg]=\mathbb E_P[(E_Sf)g]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of finite sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum_mul}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a finite index set $s$, and functions $F_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P\sum_{j\in s}F_j=\sum_{j\in s}\mathbb E_PF_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of scalar multiples]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $a\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P[af]=a\mathbb E_Pf$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product Parseval identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.parseval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_comp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.signedIntersectionEnergy, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sum_powerset_signed_inter}
\difficulty{6}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ with orthogonal components $f_S$. Then $\mathbb E_Pf^2=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\mathbb E_Pf_S^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Boolean rounding on fixed coordinates]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.exists_boolean_rounding}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.DependsOn, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.IsBoolean, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.indicator, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.prob}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, and functions $f,h:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. If $f$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$ and $h$ depends only on $J$, there exists $g:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ depending only on $J$ such that $\Pr_P(f\ne g)\le\mathbb E_P(f-h)^2$.
\end{theorem}
